title: verify and doctor
bridge: verify is like the one npm script you run before you push, which runs lint, types and the tests near your change. Except: the editor, the agent's Stop hook and CI all run the very same command. So green means the same thing in all three places, and doctor makes sure a fresh machine can run it at all.
intro: Agents and people need one fast command that gives the answer CI will give, before they say done. This lesson builds npm run verify, poe verify and the Stop hook that runs them. Then it builds poe doctor and its nightly run in the sandbox image. The backend parts are Python because fcp's backend is Django and its tooling lives in the root pyproject.toml.

picture.caption: One command per area, three callers, and a nightly proof that a fresh machine can run it.

sections.h: npm run verify for the frontend (G7-10)
p: Today a frontend change needs four commands: npm run lint, npm run check-types, the unit tests and Storybook. G7-10 adds one script, frontend/scripts/verify.ts, and "verify": "node scripts/verify.ts" in frontend/package.json. Node 24 runs .ts files directly, so there is no new .js or .mjs file.

It checks what changed since main: Biome on the changed files, the type check, and vitest related. vitest related runs only the tests that import the changed files. npm run verify -- --all checks everything; CI uses that.
sections.because: We print one line per step at the end, because the whole result must fit in an agent's context.

p: The backend version is a Poe script task in the root pyproject.toml, next to the createsuperuser task. It reads verify = { script = "scripts.poe_verify:main(all_files=all)", args = [{ name = "all", type = "boolean" }] }. A script task calls a Python function, and the boolean arg becomes a --all flag (lesson p10-6).
The first part names the areas. Some paths force the full API layer, because testmon cannot see them (lesson g7-1).
sections.because: We list the paths testmon cannot see, because a migration change must run every API test, not none.

code.text:
"""poe verify: lint and test what changed since main. The Claude Code Stop hook (scripts/claude_stop_verify.sh),
Nova's Stop hook and CI (`poe verify --all`) run this same command, so "green" means the same thing everywhere."""

import subprocess
import sys

CORE = "cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/"
CLOUD = ("cloud/rhinoCloud/", "common/fcp_common/")
FULL_RUN = (CORE + "migrations/", CORE + "fixtures/", "cloud/rhinoCloud/tests_api/conftest.py")  # testmon can't see these


def _git(*args: str) -> list[str]:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.splitlines()

sections.h: poe verify, part 2: pick, run, report
p: main() collects the changed files since the merge base plus untracked files, then builds a list of steps. Each area adds its own: lint for Python files, the API layer (all or affected), and the SDK's make targets. client/ has no fast test layer yet. Decide with the BE guild: lint client files only, or run the Docker-based unit tests.

sections.h: One Stop hook for people and Nova
p: A Stop hook is a command Claude Code runs when the agent wants to end its turn (lesson p8-4). G7-14 adds scripts/claude_stop_verify.sh and registers it in fcp's tracked .claude/settings.json. The script picks npm run verify or poe verify by changed paths. On failure it prints the summary and the failures.md path to stderr and exits 2, so Claude keeps working with that message.

If the hook input has stop_hook_active true, a stop was already blocked once. The script then reports and exits 0, so the session can end and never loops. Nova gets this hook too: its harness loads fcp's project settings (settingSources ["project"], G3-19). Nova's own Stop hook (G3-21) then only checks proof for the plan's QA checks.

CI runs the same commands. The API Tests job runs uvx --from poethepoet poe verify --all. frontend-ci's unit-tests job runs npm run verify -- --all with VITEST_MONOCART=1, in place of its separate lint, check-types and coverage steps.
sections.because: We register the hook in the tracked project settings, so every person and agent that opens fcp runs the same check.

callout.text: The command and its exit code, not shared code, are the contract between fcp and the platform's harness. Agree it with Platform: exit 0 means green, exit 1 means red, and the hook turns red into exit 2.

sections.h: poe doctor, part 1: read the requirements (G7-22)
p: Setup problems cost developers many hours a year, and agents in fresh VMs hit the same ones. G7-22 adds poe doctor: one command that checks a machine against what fcp needs and, with --fix, repairs what is safe. Its Poe entry is doctor = { script = "scripts.poe_doctor:main(fix=fix, as_json=json)", args = [...] }.
The first part reads the requirements from the repo itself, so the doctor never disagrees with the files it checks.
sections.because: We read node and npm versions from frontend/package.json engines, because a copy in the script would drift.

code.text:
"""poe doctor: check a local fcp setup; --fix runs the safe local fixes; --json is for the sandbox image build."""
import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
ENGINES = json.loads((ROOT / "frontend" / "package.json").read_text())["engines"]  # node >=24.15.0, npm >=11.14.1


def _run(*cmd: str) -> str | None:
    done = shutil.which(cmd[0]) and subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=ROOT)
    return done.stdout.strip() if done and done.returncode == 0 else None


def _at_least(have: str | None, want: str) -> bool:  # "v24.16.0" >= ">=24.15.0"
    return have is not None and [int(p) for p in have.strip("v").split(".")] >= [int(p) for p in want.strip(">=").split(".")]

notes.text: What it does and the two flags.
shutil.which finds a program on PATH, like the which command.
The repo root: two levels up from scripts/poe_doctor.py.
The engines block of frontend/package.json: node >=24.15.0, npm >=11.14.1.
Run a command from the repo root; return its output, or None if it is missing or fails.
If the program is not installed, stop here with a falsy value.
Output only on success, else None.
Compare versions as lists of numbers: v24.16.0 against >=24.15.0.
Strip v and >=, split on dots, and compare the lists number by number.

sections.h: poe doctor, part 2: checks, fixes, output
p: Each check is one line: what, a test, the fix, and whether --fix may run it. The other checks (npm, poe, the rhino-net Docker network) follow the same shape. --fix runs only safe local commands such as uv python install, make sync-deps and docker network create. It never touches credentials, ~/.aws or Docker volumes.

One check is about git hooks. After npm install, husky sets core.hooksPath to frontend/.husky/_, so the black, isort and flake8 hooks in .pre-commit-config.yaml never run on commit. The doctor reports it and points to poe verify.
sections.because: We print one JSON object per check with --json, because the nightly image build reads the result as data, not as text.

code.text:
CHECKS = [  # (what, passes, fix, safe for --fix); npm, poe and the rhino-net network follow the same pattern
    ("node " + ENGINES["node"], lambda: _at_least(_run("node", "--version"), ENGINES["node"]), "nvm install", False),
    ("Python 3.13 (uv)", lambda: _run("uv", "python", "find", "3.13"), "uv python install 3.13", True),
    ("cloud venv = uv.lock", lambda: _run("uv", "sync", "--check", "--directory", "cloud/rhinoCloud"), "make -C cloud/rhinoCloud sync-deps", True),
    ("Docker >= 16 GiB (FCP Lab)", lambda: int(_run("docker", "info", "-f", "{{.MemTotal}}") or 0) >= 16 * 2**30, "raise Docker's memory limit", False),
    ("Python commit hooks (husky owns core.hooksPath, so black/isort/flake8 never run)", lambda: _run("git", "config", "core.hooksPath") is None, "run `poe verify` before you push", False),
]


def main(fix: bool = False, as_json: bool = False) -> None:
    results = [(what, bool(passes()), how, safe) for what, passes, how, safe in CHECKS]
    for what, ok, how, safe in results:
        if fix and safe and not ok:
            subprocess.run(how, shell=True, cwd=ROOT)  # local commands only: never credentials, ~/.aws or volumes
        print(json.dumps({"check": what, "ok": ok, "fix": how}) if as_json else f"{'ok ' if ok else 'FIX'}  {what}  {'' if ok else '-> ' + how}")
    raise SystemExit(0 if all(ok for _, ok, _, _ in results) else 1)

notes.text: A table of checks: (what, passes, fix, safe for --fix).
Node's version against engines. The fix (nvm install) is not run automatically.
uv can find Python 3.13; if not, uv python install 3.13 is safe to run.
uv sync --check says whether the cloud venv matches the lockfile; make sync-deps fixes it.
docker info reports total memory in bytes; FCP Lab needs at least 16 GiB.
Passes only when core.hooksPath is unset; otherwise husky owns the hooks.
poe passes fix and as_json from the flags.
Run every check once and keep the answers.
Only safe fixes, only for failed checks, and only with --fix.
Run the fix command from the repo root; the comment repeats what it must never touch.
One JSON line per check, or a human line: ok, or FIX with the command.
Exit 0 only when every check passed.

sections.h: doctor in the nightly image build (G7-25)
p: The ai-agent-sandbox image (G3) is built every night from a brand-new machine, so it proves a fresh setup still works. G7-25 adds three Ansible tasks to its playbook, after the fcp checkout and the dependency install. Ansible is the tool that configures the machine during the Packer build (lesson p4-4).

A failing doctor fails the Packer build, so the image is not promoted and yesterday's image stays in use. The failing check names go into the G3 image-build alert, so the owner sees what broke without opening the Packer log.
sections.because: We register the doctor's output and decide later, because the report must be saved even when a check fails.

code.text:
- name: Prove a fresh fcp setup works (poe doctor)
  ansible.builtin.command:
    cmd: uvx --from poethepoet poe doctor --json
    chdir: "{{ fcp_checkout_dir }}"  # the image's fcp checkout; take the variable name from G3's playbook
  become: true
  become_user: "{{ sandbox_user }}"  # the user Nova runs as, so file ownership matches
  register: doctor
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Keep the doctor report with the image's build evidence
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    content: "{{ doctor.stdout }}"
    dest: /var/log/ai-agent-sandbox/doctor.jsonl
    mode: "0644"

- name: Fail the build, so this image is not promoted, when a check fails
  ansible.builtin.fail:
    msg: "poe doctor failed: {{ doctor.stdout_lines | map('from_json') | rejectattr('ok') | map(attribute='check') | join(', ') }}"
  when: doctor.rc != 0

Create scripts/claude_stop_verify.sh and make it executable (chmod +x):

#!/bin/bash
# Claude Code Stop hook: run verify before the agent may stop. Exit 2 sends it back to work.
input=$(cat)
if echo "$input" | grep -q '"stop_hook_active": *true'; then
  echo "verify already asked once; letting the session end" >&2
  exit 0
fi
if ! out=$(uv run poe verify 2>&1); then
  echo "$out" | grep -E '^(pass|FAIL) ' >&2
  echo "verify failed. Fix the failures above, then stop again." >&2
  exit 2
fi
exit 0

quiz.q: The Stop hook finds verify red. What should the script do?

options.text: Exit 1, so Claude Code shows an error and stops.
options.why: Exit 1 is a hook error that does not send the agent back with the message.

options.text: Print the summary and the failures.md path to stderr and exit 2.
options.why: Exit 2 blocks the stop and hands stderr to the agent as its next instruction.

options.text: Fix the failing test itself, then exit 0.
options.why: A hook reports; the agent fixes the code.

quiz.q: A change touches only cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/migrations/. What does poe verify run for the API layer?

options.text: Nothing, because no test file changed.
options.why: FULL_RUN exists for exactly this case.

options.text: poe api-test-affected, because migrations are cloud code.
options.why: testmon cannot see migrations, so the affected set could be empty.

options.text: poe api-test, the whole layer, because migrations are in FULL_RUN.
options.why: Migrations, fixtures and the conftest are read during setup, which testmon cannot track.

quiz.q: poe doctor fails in the nightly sandbox image build. What happens?

options.text: The build fails, the image is not promoted, and yesterday's image stays in use.
options.why: The alert names the failing checks so the owner can fix them.

options.text: The doctor runs --fix and the build continues.
options.why: The playbook runs the doctor without --fix; a broken fresh setup must be seen, not patched.

options.text: The new image is promoted with a warning.
options.why: Then Nova would run on a machine that cannot run verify.
